# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to export `GitHubClient` interface from http-client.ts

## So that…
internal services can use a consistent type for the GitHub HTTP transport

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GitHubClient` is exported from `src/adapters/github/internal/http-client.ts`
- [ ] `{ graphql, rest }` from `http-client.ts` satisfies `GitHubClient` without a type cast
- [ ] No other files are modified in this task

## Story Point Estimate
2

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Current State
The same dependency — the GitHub HTTP transport — is currently spelled five different ways across services:

| Service                 | Current `gh` type                                                    |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FieldValueMutator`     | `typeof graphql` (bare function)                                     |
| `LabelResolver`         | `{ graphql: typeof graphql }` (object wrapper)                       |
| `UserMilestoneResolver` | `{ graphql: typeof graphql }` (object wrapper)                       |
| `BurndownCalculator`    | `{ graphql: typeof graphql; rest: typeof rest }` (two-method object) |
| `VocabularyManager`     | `{ graphql: typeof graphql; rest: typeof rest }` (two-method object) |
| `backend.ts`            | `{ graphql: typeof graphql; rest: typeof rest }` (object)            |

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Add `GitHubClient` export to `http-client.ts`**
- Open `src/adapters/github/internal/http-client.ts`
- Add the `GitHubClient` interface after the `RestResponse` type (before the `getToken` function)
- The interface must declare `graphql<T>` and `rest<T>` as method signatures (not property arrows), matching existing function signatures exactly
- Export it as a named export

**Step 2 — Verify structural compatibility**
- Run `deno check src/index.ts` — the `{ graphql, rest }` object passed to `GitHubProjectBackend` must satisfy `GitHubClient` without any cast
- If `deno check` fails, adjust the interface to match what the functions actually accept

# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to fix `LabelResolver` for DRY violations and `hashToColor` visibility

## So that…
the service follows proper encapsulation principles

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `LabelResolver.gh` is typed `GitHubClient`
- [ ] `fetchAllLabels` is a single private method; `GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY` appears exactly once in the class
- [ ] `hashToColor` is private
- [ ] All three public label methods (`resolveLabelNodeIds`, `resolveOrCreateLabel`, `addLabel`) pass `deno check`

## Story Point Estimate
3

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: SRP + DRY + Information Hiding
Extracting `fetchAllLabels` satisfies DRY at the method level — one reason to change the network call, one place to change it. Making `hashToColor` private enforces information hiding: the class exposes _what it does_ (resolve labels, add labels), not _how it assigns colors_. Adopting `GitHubClient` for `gh` makes the service mockable.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Update `gh` field type**
- Change `private readonly gh: { graphql: typeof graphql }` to `private readonly gh: GitHubClient`
- Update the constructor parameter type to match
- Remove the `graphql` import if it is no longer referenced directly (the type comes from the interface now)
- Import `GitHubClient` from `./http-client.ts`

**Step 2 — Extract `private fetchAllLabels()`**
- Add a private method `private async fetchAllLabels(): Promise<GitHubLabel[]>` that issues `GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY` and returns `result?.repository?.labels?.nodes ?? []`
- Replace the three independent `gh.graphql(GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY, ...)` calls in `resolveLabelNodeIds`, `resolveOrCreateLabel`, and `addLabel` with `await this.fetchAllLabels()`
- Verify each method still works correctly — `fetchAllLabels` returns `GitHubLabel[]` which each method already processes

**Step 3 — Make `hashToColor` private**
- Change `hashToColor(name: string): string` to `private hashToColor(name: string): string`
- Search all files that import from `label-resolver.ts` and call `hashToColor` directly — there should be none; if any exist, move the call inside the class

**Step 4 — Verify**
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/label-resolver.ts`
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/backend.ts` to catch any breakage at the import site

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** #61 (GitHubClient interface export)
- **Unblocks:** #63 (UserMilestoneResolver)

# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to fix `UserMilestoneResolver` to adopt `RepoNodeIdProvider`

## So that…
the service follows Interface Segregation principles

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `UserMilestoneResolver` no longer has a `private fetchRepoNodeId()` method
- [ ] `UserMilestoneResolver` accepts `RepoNodeIdProvider` (not `LabelResolver`) as a constructor dependency
- [ ] `RepoNodeIdProvider` is exported and `LabelResolver` satisfies it without modification
- [ ] `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/user-milestone-resolver.ts` passes

## Story Point Estimate
3

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: ISP at the service level + narrow interface injection
TypeScript interface segregation at the service level means: accept the narrowest possible collaborator type, not a concrete class. Defining a `RepoNodeIdProvider` interface with a single method creates a focused contract. `LabelResolver` satisfies it structurally — no changes to `LabelResolver` needed.

An alternative — and simpler — solution is to pass the already-resolved `repoNodeId` as a constructor parameter. Since the server is stateless and each invocation calls `loadConfig`, the repo node ID is stable within a request. This avoids any inter-service dependency at the cost of one async call at construction time. Given the stateless-server design decision, this is the preferred approach.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Define `RepoNodeIdProvider` interface**
- Add to `src/adapters/github/internal/label-resolver.ts` (alongside `LabelResolver`) or to a new `src/adapters/github/internal/repo-node-id.ts`
- The interface has exactly one method: `fetchRepoNodeId(): Promise<string>`
- Export it
- Note: `LabelResolver` already satisfies this interface structurally — no changes to `LabelResolver` needed

**Step 2 — Update `UserMilestoneResolver` constructor**
- Open `src/adapters/github/internal/user-milestone-resolver.ts`
- Change `private readonly gh: { graphql: typeof graphql }` to `private readonly gh: GitHubClient`
- Add constructor parameter `private readonly repoNodeIdProvider: RepoNodeIdProvider`
- Import `RepoNodeIdProvider` and `GitHubClient`
- Remove the import of `graphql` from `http-client.ts` if no longer used directly

**Step 3 — Remove the duplicated private method**

content.title: [Story]: Fix FieldValueMutator — GitHubClient + parameterized mutations
content.body:
# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to fix `FieldValueMutator` to adopt `GitHubClient` and use parameterized mutations

## So that…
GraphQL mutations are type-safe and secure

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `FieldValueMutator.gh` is typed `GitHubClient`; all calls use `this.gh.graphql(...)`
- [ ] All five mutation methods (`setFieldStatus`, `setFieldSprint`, `setFieldStoryPoints`, `setFieldPriority`, `setFieldAssignee`) use named GraphQL variables — no string interpolation in mutation bodies
- [ ] All mutations have typed response generics
- [ ] `clearField` continues to use parameterized variables (already correct — do not regress)
- [ ] `deno check` passes

## Story Point Estimate
5

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: GraphQL variable parameterization — security and type safety
Embedding IDs in mutation strings via template literals bypasses GraphQL's type system. The GitHub GraphQL API enforces `ID!` types on input fields — sending a mis-formed string in an interpolated mutation produces a runtime error with no compile-time signal. Using named variables (`$itemId: ID!`) lets the API validate the type at the protocol level and gives the TypeScript generic `<ResponseType>` meaningful structure. It also eliminates the possibility of structural injection if any ID value ever comes from untrusted input.

The `clearField` method already uses parameterized variables correctly — apply the same pattern to the five remaining mutation methods.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Update `gh` field type**
- Change `private readonly gh: typeof graphql` to `private readonly gh: GitHubClient`
- Update the constructor parameter to `gh: GitHubClient`
- Replace all call sites of `this.gh(query, vars)` (bare function) with `this.gh.graphql(query, vars)`
- Import `GitHubClient` from `./http-client.ts`; remove the `graphql` function import

**Step 2 — Parameterize `setFieldStatus`**
- Remove the template literal mutation string
- Replace with a named operation `SetFieldStatus` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$optionId: String!`
- Add typed generic: `this.gh.graphql<{ updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue: { item: { id: string } } }>(...)`
- Pass `{ projectId: this.config.projectId, itemId, fieldId, optionId }` as the variables object

**Step 3 — Parameterize `setFieldSprint`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldSprint` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$iterationId: String!`
- Value type for iteration: `value: { iterationId: $iterationId }` in the mutation
- The `clearField` path (when `iterationId === null`) already uses parameterized variables — leave it as-is

**Step 4 — Parameterize `setFieldStoryPoints`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldStoryPoints` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$number: Float!`
- Note: GitHub Projects v2 uses `Float!` (not `Int!`) for number field values
- The `clearField` null-path is already parameterized — leave as-is

**Step 5 — Parameterize `setFieldPriority`**
- Named operation: `SetFieldPriority` with variables `$projectId: ID!`, `$itemId: ID!`, `$fieldId: ID!`, `$optionId: String!`
- Same structure as `SetFieldStatus`

**Step 6 — Parameterize `setFieldAssignee`**
- Named operation `ClearAssignees` for the null path: variables `$issueId: ID!`, value `assigneeIds: []`
- Named operation `SetAssignee` for the set path: variables `$issueId: ID!`, `$userId: ID!`
- Note: `issueId` here is an issue node ID (not a project item ID) — this is correct as-is; keep the parameter name `$issueId`

**Step 7 — Verify**
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/field-value-mutator.ts`
- Confirm no bare template literal mutations remain in the file (`grep '`\`mutation {' field-value-mutator.ts` should return nothing)

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** #61 (GitHubClient interface)
- **Unblocks:** F.2.1 (facade wiring), which unblocks #54, #55

content.title: [Story]: Rewrite BurndownCalculator
content.body:
# User Story

## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…
developer

## I want…
to rewrite `BurndownCalculator` from scratch

## So that…
it follows DRY principles and uses existing abstractions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] File passes `deno check` with no errors
- [ ] `getBurndownInput` uses `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher` from `pagination.ts` — no custom pagination
- [ ] `resolveCompletionTimestamps` reads `response.data` as a direct array — not `response.data.events`
- [ ] Zero `any` types in the file
- [ ] `resolveSprint` and `buildBurndownStoryInput` are imported, not re-implemented

## Story Point Estimate
5

## Affected component
GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Additional context / notes
### Why: DRY + Dependency Inversion + eliminating `any`
The three re-implementations (`resolveSprint`, `fetchAllItems`, `buildBurndownStoryInput`) each violate DRY. If the pagination logic or mapping logic changes, `BurndownCalculator` would diverge silently. The correct design: depend on the already-extracted abstractions, not on duplicated copies.

Eliminating `any` at the mapping boundary is required because `buildBurndownStoryInput` in `mappers.ts` already has the correct type for the raw project item — use its input type, not `any`.

### Implementation Steps
**Step 1 — Delete the current file body (keep the header comment)**
- Open `src/adapters/github/internal/burndown-calculator.ts`
- Delete all class body content below the file header comment
- Keep the imports section — it will be rewritten

**Step 2 — Write the correct constructor**
```typescript
import { GitHubClient } from "./http-client.ts";
import { PaginatedProjectItemFetcher } from "./pagination.ts";
import { buildBurndownStoryInput } from "../mappers.ts";
import { resolveSprint } from "./resolver.ts"; // standalone function — not a class method
import type { RuntimeConfig } from "../config-loader.ts";
import type {
  BurndownInput,
  BurndownStoryInput,
  CompletionMap,
  SprintInfo,
} from "../../../scrum/ports.ts";
import type { SprintRef } from "../../../domain/types.ts";

export class BurndownCalculator {
  constructor(
    private readonly config: RuntimeConfig,
    private readonly gh: GitHubClient,
    private readonly owner: string,
    private readonly repo: string,
  ) {}
}
```

**Step 3 — Implement `getBurndownInput(sprint: SprintRef)`**
- Call `resolveSprint(sprint, this.config)` — the standalone function from `resolver.ts`; capture the returned `iterationId: string | null`
- If `iterationId === null`, throw `new Error("Burndown does not apply to the backlog.")`
- Find the iteration entry: `this.config.iterations.all.find((i) => i.id === iterationId)` — throw if not found
- Create a `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher` instance using `this.config`, `{ graphql: this.gh.graphql }`, and appropriate options (same options as `getBacklogStories` in `backend.ts` — include `sprintFieldIds`, `includeIssueContent: true`)
- Call `fetcher.collect()` with a filter predicate that checks `item.fieldValues.nodes` for a field matching `this.config.fields.sprintFieldId` with `iterationId`
- Map filtered items with `buildBurndownStoryInput(item, this.config)` from `mappers.ts`
- Filter out nulls: `.filter((s): s is BurndownStoryInput => s !== null)`
- Compute `endDate` from `iterEntry.startDate + iterEntry.duration` days
- Return `BurndownInput` with `sprint: SprintInfo` and `stories: BurndownStoryInput[]`

**Step 4 — Implement `resolveCompletionTimestamps(input: BurndownInput)`**
- Iterate `input.stories` — for each story with a `number`, call the REST timeline endpoint
- Correct REST path: `repos/${this.owner}/${this.repo}/issues/${story.number}/timeline`
- Correct response shape: `response.data` IS the array — type it as `Array<{ event: string; created_at: string }>`
- Filter for `event === "closed"` where `created_at` falls within `[sprint.startDate, sprint.endDate]`
- Record the last such timestamp in a `Map<number, string>`
- Wrap each story in `try/catch` and `continue` on failure (individual timeline fetch errors should not abort the whole burndown)
- Return `CompletionMap` with `dataSource: "issue_close_proxy"` and the standard warning string

**Step 5 — Verify**
- Run `deno check src/adapters/github/internal/burndown-calculator.ts`
- Confirm no `any` types appear in the file
- Confirm `resolveSprint` is imported from `./resolver.ts`, not defined as a private method
- Confirm `buildBurndownStoryInput` is imported from `../mappers.ts`, not defined as a private method
- Confirm `fetchAllItems` does NOT exist as a method in the class

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** F.0 (GitHubClient interface)
- **Unblocks:** F.2.1

No formal `StoryType`, `TemplateField`, or `ItemTemplate` discriminated union exists in the innermost domain layer.

Domain layer (src/domain/)

Inconsistent template handling, increased coupling between use cases and concrete template formats, and inability to support GitHub Issue Form YML parsing without violating clean architecture principles.

## Expected behaviour

The diagram generator (`scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts`) correctly identifies all imported names from multi-line import statements, so that `docs/proj-diagram.md` reports only genuinely unused exports.

## Actual behaviour

`extractImportedNames()` uses `lines.find()` to locate the single line containing `from '...'`. For multi-line imports, the matched line is `} from "..."`, which contains no `{...}` destructuring block — so none of the imported names are captured. Every export that is only imported via a multi-line statement is reported as unused.

**False positives observed:** `BurndownResponse`, `BurndownSprintMeta`, `ItemContentType`, all `ports.ts` boundary types, all `queries.ts`/`mappers.ts` exports, all `schemas/scrum.ts` schemas.

**Location:** [`scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts`](scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Locate any file in the project that uses a multi-line import (spread over more than one line)
2. Run the diagram generator
3. Observe that every name from the multi-line import block appears as an "unused export" in `docs/proj-diagram.md`

## Affected MCP tool

Other / unknown — defect is in the `scripts/diagram/` tooling, not the `scrum_*` tool surface.

## Severity

Minor – cosmetic or edge-case issue

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace single-line `lines.find()` with a loop that collects full multi-line import statements in `extractImportedNames()`
- [ ] Join the collected lines and apply regex on the joined string to handle multi-line imports
- [ ] Run diagram generator and verify false positives are eliminated
- [ ] Regenerate `docs/proj-diagram.md` with accurate unused-export analysis

content.title: Per-Item Start Dates & Delivery Deadlines with Extension Tracking
content.body:
## User Story

As a developer using the scrum master agent, I want to set a start date and an expected delivery date on any backlog item, so that the agent can flag items that are overdue, prioritize work by approaching deadlines even when the item's priority tier is lower, and always log the reason when a delivery date is pushed out — preserving a full history of every date change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Items can carry a start date (when work is expected to begin) and an expected delivery date (when the item should be Done)
- [ ] The SM agent proactively surfaces overdue items (past their expected delivery date) during every board health check
- [ ] When an item's delivery date is approaching — even if it carries a lower priority tier — the agent flags it as needing attention before higher-priority but later-deadline items
- [ ] Every deadline extension is documented: the agent captures the reason for the delay as a comment on the item before the date field is changed
- [ ] The agent surfaces items with no expected delivery date as a planning gap during refinement and sprint planning

## Non-Goals

- Automatic priority reassignment based on deadlines (the agent can flag tension between deadline urgency and priority tier, but priority is always a human decision)
- Sprint-level deadline enforcement (the sprint end date is tracked separately via burndown)

Human using the agent

The agent to show me the full dependency picture for a set of items in a single response

- [ ] When `include_dependencies: true`, the response includes a `DependencyMap` keyed by issue number (`key`) covering all items in the result set plus any out-of-scope dependencies they reference

## As a…
Human using the agent

## I want…
The agent to automatically fetch and apply the right template when creating a new backlog item

## So that…
Every item the agent creates is consistently structured for its type, without me having to paste or reference a template manually

- [ ] The agent discovers available URIs from `vocabulary.template_uris` in the orient response (from #143) — no separate resource listing call is needed

## Additional context

Depends on #143 (template URI map), #86 (template file paths in config), #83 (FileReader port for reading template files), and #84 (config-relative path resolution). As a **developer adding a new backend integration**, I want **an `AbstractAssembler` base class with port method defaults**, so that **I only implement assembly and normalization methods — the execute + return pattern is provided**.

content.title: [User Story]: Agent receives actionable error guidance — BackendError subclasses with recoverySuggestion
content.body:
### User Story

As an **agent user**, I want to receive **actionable error guidance from the backend** (typed `BackendError` subclasses with recovery suggestions), so that **I can recover from errors without seeing raw stack traces or cryptic HTTP status codes**.

### Problem

Raw HTTP/GraphQL errors surface as generic strings or stack traces. The agent can't interpret whether an error is an auth issue (check the token), a rate limit (retry in X seconds), a capability gap (try a different approach), or a platform constraint (results are partial).

### Solution

Implement the error decoration hierarchy:

```
BackendError (base)
BackendAuthError          — token missing/expired → check env var
CapabilityUnavailableError — op can't be expressed → try alternative
CapabilityEmulationWarning — op works with encoding conventions
PlatformConstraintError    — partial/reduced fidelity result
BackendRateLimitError      — retry after X seconds
```

The abstract assembler's `execute()` wrapper catches raw errors from the execution engine and re-throws them as typed `BackendError` subclasses. Each carries a `recoverySuggestion` the agent can surface to the user.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `BackendError` base class with `capability`, `platform`, `recoverySuggestion`, `platformContext` fields
- [ ] All five error subclasses implemented with appropriate `recoverySuggestion` defaults
- [ ] `AbstractAssembler.execute()` wraps raw errors into typed subclasses
- [ ] Use-case functions catch `CapabilityUnavailableError` → surface in `warnings[]`
- [ ] Fatal errors produce structured error strings (not stack traces) in tool responses
- [ ] Agent never sees a raw HTTP status code or GraphQL error

### Dependencies
- [ ] AbstractAssembler implemented
- [ ] CapabilityStatus enum exists

Only authorised agents can access the server in a multi-client deployment, preventing unauthorised use of shared server infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The server acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource server — it rejects unauthenticated requests with `HTTP 401 Unauthorized` and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header
- [ ] The server validates access tokens on every HTTP request — tokens must be issued specifically for this server (audience check); invalid or expired tokens receive `HTTP 401`
- [ ] The server returns `HTTP 403 Forbidden` with `error="insufficient_scope"` when a token is valid but lacks the required scopes for the requested operation
- [ ] The server implements OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) — either via `WWW-Authenticate` header or a well-known URI — so clients can discover the authorization server
- [ ] The server supports the `resource` parameter (RFC 8707) for token audience binding on authorization and token requests
- [ ] Configuration flag `--auth` enables auth mode; default is unauthenticated (backwards-compatible with existing `stdio` usage)
- [ ] Auth mode is documented: supported flows (authorization code + PKCE), token validation rules, authorization server discovery URL, and scope requirements

## Story Point Estimate

5

## Affected component

MCP tool surface (scrum_* tools)

## Additional context / notes

**Dependencies:**
- **Depends on:** #93 (Run the server in Streamable HTTP mode — HTTP transport must exist before auth can be layered on)
- **Belongs to epic:** Streamable HTTP Transport Mode with Per-Connection Config Override

**Reference:** [MCP Authorization Spec (2025-11-25)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization) — OAuth 2.1-based, requires PKCE S256, token audience validation, and resource parameter. SSE transport is deprecated; this applies to Streamable HTTP only.

content.title: [Bug]: Org-level GitHub Issue Fields silently dropped from all read paths
content.body:
## Description
Org-level GitHub Issue Fields (Priority, Effort, custom single-select/text/number/date fields) added as project board columns have their values silently dropped by the GitHub adapter. The GitHub GraphQL API returns these values as `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` nodes, but the adapter has zero handling for this type across five layers — meaning every read path (item listing, story detail, board health, analytics) loses those field values entirely.

Reference: [GitHub Community Discussion #189141 — Issue fields: Structured issue metadata is in public preview](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/189141)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable org-level issue fields in an organization's GitHub settings (Settings → Planning → Issue fields)
2. Add one or more issue fields (e.g., Priority, Effort) as columns to a GitHub Project V2 board
3. Set field values on issues already tracked in the project
4. Call `scrum_find_items` or `scrum_get_item_detail` via the MCP server
5. Observe: the issue field values are absent from all responses

## Expected Behaviour
All project field values are returned, including values originating from org-level issue fields. The adapter should unwrap `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` nodes and expose their inner values (single-select, text, number, or date) as regular field values.

## Actual Behaviour
`ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` nodes are silently dropped at five layers:

### Layer 1 — GraphQL fragment (`src/adapters/github/operations.graphql`)
The `ItemFieldValues` fragment (line 122) selects inline fragments for 9 legacy field value types but has **no `... on ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue`** inline fragment. The response nodes land in GraphQL's response but are never matched.

### Layer 2 — TypeScript interface (`src/adapters/github/types.ts`)
`ItemFieldValue` (line 314) has no `issueFieldValue` property. The `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` type wraps its value inside `issueFieldValue: IssueFieldDateValue | IssueFieldNumberValue | IssueFieldSingleSelectValue | IssueFieldTextValue` — a completely different nesting shape than the flat `name`/`optionId`/`number` on traditional field values.

### Layer 3 — Field extraction (`src/adapters/github/mappers.ts`)
`extractBoardFields` (line 106) receives nodes typed as `FieldValueNode` which only exposes `field.id`, `name`, `title`, `number` as flat properties. For `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue`, the single-select display name lives inside `fv.issueFieldValue.name` — one level deeper, and the type system doesn't even model it.

### Layer 4 — Custom fields passthrough (`src/adapters/github/internal/result-normalizer.ts`)
`enrichListingCustomFields` (line 18) iterates field value nodes and serializes flat properties (`iterationId`, `title`, `text`, `number`, `name`, `optionId`, etc.) into the `custom_fields` map. `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` has none of these at the top level — the inner `issueFieldValue` is never reached.

### Layer 5 — Write path (`src/adapters/github/internal/field-value-mutator.ts`)
All mutations use the `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` mutation. For issue-backed project fields, the correct mutation is `setIssueFieldValue` / `updateIssueFieldValue` (from the Issue Fields REST/GraphQL API). Writing values to issue-backed fields via the wrong mutation may silently fail.

## Environment
- **Component:** GitHub adapter (all read + write paths)
- **Affected tools:** `scrum_find_items`, `scrum_get_item_detail`, `scrum_get_board_health`, `scrum_get_analytics`, `scrum_set_field`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` inline fragment added to `ItemFieldValues` in `operations.graphql`, selecting the four nested `ProjectV2IssueFieldValues` union members (`IssueFieldDateValue`, `IssueFieldNumberValue`, `IssueFieldSingleSelectValue`, `IssueFieldTextValue`) via the `issueFieldValue` field
- [ ] `ItemFieldValue` TypeScript interface extended with an `issueFieldValue` property typed to the appropriate nested union
- [ ] `extractBoardFields` unwraps single-select/date/number/text values from the nested `issueFieldValue` structure, mapping by `field.id` against the resolved field IDs from bootstrap
- [ ] `enrichListingCustomFields` serializes `ProjectV2ItemIssueFieldValue` inner values into the `custom_fields` passthrough
- [ ] Write path uses `setIssueFieldValue` / `updateIssueFieldValue` mutations for fields identified as issue-backed (by matching field name against issue fields returned from the org-level API)
- [ ] Existing tests pass; field values from legacy (non-issue) project fields continue to work unchanged

content.title: [Bug]: scrum_find_items blocked_by entries omit title — agents cannot identify blockers without extra round-trips
content.body:
## Problem

In `scrum_find_items` responses, `blocked_by` entries contain only `{ id, key }` — the blocker's title is absent. An agent reading a listing response cannot identify what is blocking an item without making additional `scrum_get_item_detail` calls.

**scrum_find_items blocked_by (current):**
```json
"blocked_by": [{ "id": "I_kwDO...", "key": "185" }]
```

**scrum_get_item_detail blocked_by (correct shape):**
```json
"blocked_by": [{ "key": "185", "title": "[Tech Debt]: Extract fragment library...", "ref": { "id": "..." } }]
```

The item title is available in the fetched data at listing build time — the listing normalizer does not include it.

## Impact

During dependency chain analysis (grooming, sprint planning, impediment review), an agent holding only a `scrum_find_items` response cannot understand what is blocking what without extra round-trips — one `scrum_get_item_detail` call per unique blocker key encountered. This cost was observed directly during grooming session 2026-06-03.

## Affected file

`src/adapters/github/internal/result-normalizer.ts` — `blocked_by` mapping in `toItemListing()`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `blocked_by` entries in `scrum_find_items` responses include a `title` field
- [ ] Shape matches `scrum_get_item_detail` blocked_by: `{ key, title, ref }`
- [ ] No additional API calls required to identify blockers from a listing response
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new test covers title presence in `blocked_by` listing entries

content.title: [Bug]: scrum_find_items blocks field always empty — downstream dependency impact invisible, dead field on every item
content.body:
## Problem

Every item in `scrum_find_items` carries `"blocks": []` regardless of actual dependency relationships. The server populates `blocked_by` (upstream dependencies) by reading each item's own data. It never computes the reverse — which items this item is blocking downstream.

The field is present on every response item but semantically empty on all of them. This has two costs:

**1. Agents cannot determine downstream blast radius.**
If an item is resolved or re-prioritized, an agent cannot tell from the listing which downstream items are affected or become unblocked. This information is needed for sprint planning and impediment resolution.

**2. Dead field on every item.**
`"blocks": []` appears on every item in every `scrum_find_items` response — wasted context with no signal.

## Impact

Sprint planning and impediment resolution both benefit from knowing downstream dependencies. Currently this information is unavailable from any listing tool. Agents working from `scrum_find_items` output have no path to downstream impact analysis.

## Design decision required

Two valid resolutions — decision should be made before implementation:

**(a) Compute `blocks` via cross-reference:** after fetching all items, build a reverse map from each item's `blocked_by` entries. O(n), no extra API calls. Accurate only for items present in the fetched set — may be incomplete under pagination.

**(b) Remove `blocks` from listing schema:** omit the field entirely. Honest representation of a server-side gap. `scrum_get_item_detail` can still expose downstream dependencies if that tool's response is extended.

Option (b) is recommended if the fetched set may be a subset of all board items, since a partial cross-reference produces a misleading graph.

## Affected files

- `src/adapters/github/internal/result-normalizer.ts` — `toItemListing()` / listing schema
- `src/scrum/ports.ts` / `src/domain/types.ts` — `BacklogItemListing` type if field is removed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `blocks` is either accurately populated in listing responses, or removed from the listing schema entirely
- [ ] No silent empty arrays — either real data or field absent
- [ ] If removed from listing: `scrum_get_item_detail` still exposes downstream dependencies where available
- [ ] Existing tests updated to reflect whichever resolution is chosen
